reason: All five FR-10 normative requirements are pinned by assertions: (a) Content-Type=application/problem+json for 422/404/429 (test_fr10.py:289) and 500 (test_fr10.py:476); (b) body fields type/title/status/detail (test_fr10.py:322-327) plus instance+correlation_id at serializer (test_fr10.py:636-647); (c) no internal-detail leak — Traceback (test_fr10.py:426), file path (test_fr10.py:446), SQL (test_fr10.py:457), schema (test_fr10.py:461); (d) X-Correlation-Id header AND audit log (test_fr10.py:540-550 and test_fr10.py:570-579); (e) error-code map for 422/401/403/404/409/429/503/500 (test_fr10.py:678-698).

gaps.message: 401/403/409/503 Content-Type on HTTP wire is only verified at the unit-class status-attribute level (test_concrete_problem_subclasses_match_ac_10_5_error_code_map); the FR-10 AC-10.1 wire assertion (Content-Type: application/problem+json) only runs for 422/404/429/500, leaving four status codes without an HTTP-level Content-Type guard.

Integration test asserts body contains type/title/status/detail only; instance and correlation_id are only verified at the problem_body serializer level (test_problem_body_serializes_all_wire_fields). An HTTP handler that filters these fields out would not be caught by the integration test.

Tautological if-triggers such as `assert expected_status == "422"` (line 276), `assert content_type == "application/problem+json"` (line 287), `assert forbidden_pattern == "Traceback"` (line 422), `assert expected_hits == "0"` (line 434), `assert header_name == "X-Correlation-Id"` (line 539), `assert expected_match == "true"` (line 565) only mirror the parametrize/literal value and never fail regardless of implementation; the real checks follow on the next line.
